questionText: 17th of month is Saturday. First day of month was?
hints: The same day of the week comes back every 7 days. Use this to jump backwards from the date you know.
Take 7 away from 17, and then 7 again, to find earlier Saturdays. Then count back the last few days to the 1st.

Similar example: the 20th is a Wednesday. Going back in 7s, the 13th and the 6th are also Wednesdays. Counting back from the 6th: the 5th is Tuesday, the 4th Monday, the 3rd Sunday, the 2nd Saturday and the 1st Friday.

stepByStep.text: Go back 7 days. The 10th is also a Saturday.
Go back 7 more days. The 3rd is also a Saturday.
Count back from the 3rd: the 2nd is a Friday and the 1st is a Thursday.
So the first day of the month was Thursday.

misconceptions.A: Friday is the 2nd, the day before Saturday the 3rd. Go back one more day to reach the 1st.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The 3rd is a Saturday, so the 2nd is Friday and the 1st is Thursday.
misconceptions.C: Check your counting back. The 3rd is a Saturday, so the 2nd is Friday and the 1st is the day before that.
misconceptions.D: Sunday comes after Saturday. Here we go backwards from Saturday the 3rd to reach the 1st.

questionText: At half past six, angle between hour and minute hand?
hints: On a clock the hour hand does not sit still. It creeps forward as the minutes pass. Find where each hand points, then find the gap between them.
The gap between two neighbouring numbers on a clock is 30°. At half past six the minute hand is on 6. Think about where the hour hand is between 6 and 7.

Similar example: at 20 minutes past 8, the minute hand is on 4. In 60 minutes the hour hand moves 30°, so in 20 minutes it moves 10° past the 8. From 4 to 8 is 4 × 30 = 120°. The angle is 120 + 10 = 130°.

stepByStep.text: The 12 numbers on a clock share a full turn of 360°. So each gap between numbers is 30°.
At half past six the minute hand points exactly at 6.
Half an hour has passed since 6 o'clock, so the hour hand has moved halfway from 6 to 7.
Half of one gap is the angle between the hands. The angle is 15°.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The hour hand is half a gap past 6, and half of 30° is 15°.
misconceptions.B: Check the size of one gap. Each gap between clock numbers is 30°, and the hour hand is half a gap past 6.
misconceptions.C: This is one full gap. The hour hand is only halfway from 6 to 7, so the angle is half of this.
misconceptions.D: This is one and a half gaps. The hour hand is only half a gap away from the minute hand at 6.

questionText: In 300 seconds the minute hand moves ___ degrees?
hints: Change the seconds into minutes first. Then think about how far the minute hand turns in one minute.
There are 60 seconds in a minute, so find 300 ÷ 60. The minute hand goes all the way round, 360°, in 60 minutes.
Similar example: in 900 seconds, 900 ÷ 60 = 15 minutes pass. The minute hand turns 360 ÷ 60 = 6° each minute. So it turns 15 × 6 = 90°.

stepByStep.text: Change 300 seconds into minutes.
The minute hand makes a full turn of 360° in 60 minutes. Find its turn in 1 minute.
In 5 minutes it turns 5 times as much. The minute hand moves 30 degrees.

misconceptions.A: This is half of 300. First change 300 seconds to 5 minutes, then use 6° for each minute.
misconceptions.B: That is the turn in 10 minutes. 300 seconds is only 5 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 300 seconds is 5 minutes, and 5 × 6 = 30.
misconceptions.D: This is half of the real turn. The minute hand moves 6° every minute, and 5 minutes pass.

questionText: 1st Jan 2006 = Sunday. 1st Jan 2010?
hints: An ordinary year has 365 days, which is 52 full weeks and 1 extra day. So the same date moves forward one weekday each year, and two after a leap year.
Go one year at a time from 1st January 2006. Check which of the years 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 is a leap year.

Similar example: 1st January 2014 was a Wednesday. 2014 and 2015 are ordinary years, so 1st January 2015 is a Thursday and 1st January 2016 is a Friday. 2016 is a leap year, so the day moves on by 2: 1st January 2017 is a Sunday.

stepByStep.text: An ordinary year is 52 weeks and 1 day, so a date moves on by 1 weekday.
2006 is an ordinary year, so 1st January 2007 is a Monday. 2007 is ordinary too, so 1st January 2008 is a Tuesday.
2008 is a leap year with 366 days, so the day moves on by 2. 1st January 2009 is a Thursday.
2009 is an ordinary year. So 1st January 2010 is a Friday.

misconceptions.A: This moves one day too many. Only 2008 is a leap year, so the day moves 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 days on from Sunday.
misconceptions.B: This moves 4 days, one for each year. 2008 is a leap year, so it adds one extra day.
misconceptions.C: That is the day one year later, in 2007. Keep going for all four years.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The day moves 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 days on from Sunday, which is Friday.

questionText: Teacher: angle between hands=45°. What time?
hints: Each gap between numbers on a clock is 30°. Remember that the hour hand creeps forward as the minutes pass. Test each time.
Start with the half-past times. The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between two numbers. Count the gaps between the hands.

Similar example: what is the angle at 3:30? The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. From the hour hand to 4 is half a gap, 15°. From 4 to 6 is 2 × 30 = 60°. The angle is 15 + 60 = 75°.

stepByStep.text: Each gap between clock numbers is 30°.
At 7:30 the minute hand is on 6. The hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8.
From 6 to 7 is one gap of 30°. From 7 to the hour hand is half a gap, 15°.
Add them. The angle is 45°, so the time is 07:30.

misconceptions.A: At 1:15 the minute hand is on 3 and the hour hand is a little past 1. That angle is more than 45°. Try a half-past time.
misconceptions.B: At 2:30 the hands are three and a half gaps apart, which is 105°. Look for hands one and a half gaps apart.
misconceptions.C: At 8:30 the hands are two and a half gaps apart, which is 75°. Look for hands one and a half gaps apart.
misconceptions.D: Yes! At 7:30 the hands are one and a half gaps apart, and 30 + 15 = 45.

questionText: Weeks in 8×7×6×5×4×3×2×1 minutes?
hints: Change minutes into hours, hours into days, and days into weeks. Take it one unit at a time.
First multiply out the product to get the number of minutes. Then divide by 60 to change the minutes into hours.
Similar example: how many weeks are in 20160 minutes? 20160 ÷ 60 = 336 hours. 336 ÷ 24 = 14 days. 14 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks.

stepByStep.text: Multiply out the minutes.
Change minutes to hours.
Change hours to days.
Change days to weeks. There are 4 weeks.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 40320 minutes is 672 hours, which is 28 days, and 28 ÷ 7 = 4.
misconceptions.B: Check the last step. The minutes make 28 days, and 28 ÷ 7 gives the weeks.
misconceptions.C: Check the multiplication first. The product is 40320 minutes, which is 672 hours.
misconceptions.D: This is one week too many. The minutes make 28 days, and 7 days make a week.

questionText: It is 4:30pm on April 15th. Minute hand turns 30 times. What date and time?
hints: One full turn of the minute hand takes one hour. So count the turns as hours and move the clock forward.
30 turns means 30 hours. Split 30 hours into one full day of 24 hours and the hours left over.
Similar example: it is 9:00 am on 3rd May and the minute hand turns 28 times. That is 28 hours, and 24 + 4 = 28. After 24 hours it is 9:00 am on 4th May. Four more hours make it 1:00 pm on 4th May.

stepByStep.text: Each full turn of the minute hand is 1 hour. So 30 turns is 30 hours.
Split 30 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 4:30 pm on 15th April is 4:30 pm on 16th April.
6 hours after that is 10:30 pm. So it is 10:30pm, 16th April.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 30 turns is 30 hours: one full day and 6 hours more.
misconceptions.B: After full turns the minute hand is back where it started, on the 6. So the time must end in 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: This adds 42 hours. 30 turns is 30 hours: one full day and 6 more hours.
misconceptions.D: This moves on many days. 30 turns of the minute hand is only 30 hours, a little more than one day.

questionText: Time 2023 minutes after 12:00am on 2nd March 2023?
hints: Change the minutes into hours and minutes. Then see whether the hours go past one full day.
Divide 2023 by 60 to get the hours and the leftover minutes. Remember that a day has 24 hours.
Similar example: 1500 minutes after 12:00 am on 5th June. 1500 ÷ 60 = 25 hours. 24 hours takes us to 12:00 am on 6th June, and 1 more hour makes it 1:00 am on 6th June.

stepByStep.text: 60 minutes make an hour. 33 hours use up 1980 minutes.
Find the minutes left over. So 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes.
Split 33 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 12:00 am on 2nd March is 12:00 am on 3rd March.
9 hours 43 minutes later it is 3rd March 9:43 am.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes: one full day, then 9 hours 43 minutes more.
misconceptions.B: That is only 21 hours 43 minutes after midnight. 2023 minutes is 33 hours 43 minutes, more than a full day.
misconceptions.C: The date is right, but 9 hours after midnight is still morning.
misconceptions.D: This goes one day too far. 33 hours is one full day and 9 hours.

questionText: Angle between hour and minute hand at 8:30 am?
hints: On a clock the hour hand does not sit still. It creeps forward as the minutes pass. Find where each hand points, then count the gaps between them.
Each gap between clock numbers is 30°. At 8:30 the minute hand is on 6. Think about where the hour hand is between 8 and 9.
Similar example: at 2:30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3. From the hour hand to 3 is half a gap, 15°. From 3 to 6 is 3 × 30 = 90°. The angle is 15 + 90 = 105°.

stepByStep.text: Each gap between clock numbers is 30°.
At 8:30 the minute hand is on 6. The hour hand is halfway between 8 and 9.
From 6 to 8 is two gaps.
The hour hand is half a gap, 15°, past 8.
The angle is 75°, which is not listed. So the answer is none of these.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The angle is 60° + 15° = 75°, and 75° is not one of the angles given.
misconceptions.B: Check the half gap. The hour hand is 15° past 8, and the two full gaps make 60°.
misconceptions.C: This counts three full gaps, as if the hour hand were on 9. At 8:30 it is only halfway from 8 to 9.
misconceptions.D: Check the adding. Two gaps make 60°, and the half gap adds 15° more.

questionText: Republic Day 2023 = Thursday. Which year on Tuesday?
hints: Republic Day is 26th January. Each ordinary year the day moves forward by 1, and by 2 when a 29th February falls in between.
Go year by year from 26th January 2023. Watch for the leap year 2024: its extra day, 29th February, comes after Republic Day 2024.
Similar example: 26th January 2015 was a Monday. In 2016 it is a Tuesday. From January 2016 to January 2017 we pass 29th February 2016, so it moves 2 days to a Thursday. In 2018 it is a Friday.

stepByStep.text: Republic Day is 26th January. In an ordinary year the same date moves on by 1 weekday.
From 2023 to 2024 there is no leap day in between. So 26th January 2024 is a Friday.
From 2024 to 2025 we pass 29th February 2024, so the day moves on by 2. 26th January 2025 is a Sunday.
Then 2026 gives Monday and 2027 gives Tuesday.
So Republic Day falls on a Tuesday in 2027.

misconceptions.A: In 2026 it falls on a Monday. Go one more year.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The days go Friday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday for 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.
misconceptions.C: In 2028 it falls on a Wednesday. That is one year too far.
misconceptions.D: In 2025 it falls on a Sunday. Keep moving forward one day each year.

questionText: 10:30am on 21st April 2024. Minute hand turns 42 times. Date and time?
hints: One full turn of the minute hand takes one hour. So count the turns as hours and move the clock forward.
42 turns means 42 hours. Split 42 hours into one full day of 24 hours and the hours left over.

Similar example: it is 7:00 am on 10th July and the minute hand turns 40 times. That is 40 hours, and 24 + 16 = 40. After 24 hours it is 7:00 am on 11th July. Sixteen more hours make it 11:00 pm on 11th July.

stepByStep.text: Each full turn of the minute hand is 1 hour. So 42 turns is 42 hours.
Split 42 hours into 1 day and some hours.
24 hours after 10:30 am on 21st April is 10:30 am on 22nd April.
12 hours more makes it 10:30 pm on 22nd April. There are still 6 hours to add.
6 hours after 10:30 pm is 4:30 am the next day. So it is 23rd Apr 4:30am.

misconceptions.A: This goes too far. 42 hours is one full day and 18 hours, which ends early on the 23rd.
misconceptions.B: The time is right but the date is one day too late. 42 hours is less than two full days.
misconceptions.C: This adds only 34 hours. 42 turns of the minute hand is 42 hours.
misconceptions.D: Yes! 42 hours is one full day and 18 hours more, which reaches 4:30 am on the 23rd.

questionText: Independence Day 2024 = Thursday. Which year on Wednesday?
hints: Independence Day is 15th August. Each ordinary year the day moves forward by 1, and by 2 when a 29th February falls in between.
Go year by year from 15th August 2024. Watch for the next leap year, 2028: its 29th February makes the day jump by 2.
Similar example: 15th August 2014 was a Friday. In 2015 it is a Saturday. From August 2015 to August 2016 we pass 29th February 2016, so it moves 2 days to a Monday. In 2017 it is a Tuesday.

stepByStep.text: Independence Day is 15th August. In an ordinary year the same date moves on by 1 weekday.
So 2025 gives Friday, 2026 gives Saturday and 2027 gives Sunday.
From August 2027 to August 2028 we pass 29th February 2028, so the day moves on by 2. 15th August 2028 is a Tuesday.
One more year gives Wednesday. So Independence Day falls on a Wednesday in 2029.

misconceptions.A: In 2028 it falls on a Tuesday, because the leap day makes the day jump on from Sunday. Go one more year.
misconceptions.B: In 2030 it falls on a Thursday. That is one year too far.
misconceptions.C: In 2031 it falls on a Friday. Count on from Thursday one year at a time, with a jump of 2 for 2028.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The days go Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday for 2025 to 2029.

questionText: 15th August 2024 was a Thursday. Which of these days came 5 times in that month?
hints: A day comes 5 times in a month only if it falls on the first few dates. Find how many days the month has and which day it started on.
Count back from the 15th in jumps of 7 to find the day of 1st August. Then remember that August has 31 days, which is 4 full weeks and 3 days more.
Similar example: a month of 30 days starts on a Monday. 30 days is 4 full weeks and 2 days more, so only the first two days, Monday and Tuesday, come 5 times.

stepByStep.text: Count back in sevens from the 15th. The 8th and the 1st are also Thursdays.
August has 31 days, which is 4 full weeks and 3 days more.
The 3 extra dates are the 29th, 30th and 31st. They fall on Thursday, Friday and Saturday, so these three days come 5 times.
Of the days given, the one that came 5 times is Saturday.

misconceptions.A: Yes! August 2024 began on a Thursday, so Thursday, Friday and Saturday each came 5 times. The Saturdays were 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31.
misconceptions.B: The Mondays were 5, 12, 19 and 26, which is 4 times. One more Monday would need a 33rd day in the month.
misconceptions.C: The 15th was a Thursday, so the 14th was a Wednesday. The Wednesdays were 7, 14, 21 and 28, which is 4 times.
misconceptions.D: The Sundays were 4, 11, 18 and 25, which is 4 times. Only the first three days of the month, Thursday, Friday and Saturday, come 5 times.

questionText: Bus from Pune to Mumbai every 36 min from 7am. Arrive 8:50am. Next bus?
hints: List the bus times one after another. The next bus is the first one that leaves after you arrive.
Start at 7:00 am and keep adding 36 minutes: 7:36 am, and so on. Stop when you pass 8:50 am.
Similar example: buses leave every 25 minutes from 6:00 am, and you arrive at 7:20 am. The buses leave at 6:00, 6:25, 6:50, 7:15 and 7:40. The 7:15 bus has gone, so the next bus is at 7:40 am.

stepByStep.text: The buses leave at 7:00 am, 7:36 am, 8:12 am and 8:48 am.
The 8:48 am bus has just left when you arrive at 8:50 am.
Add 36 minutes to 8:48 am. 48 and 36 make 84 minutes, which is 1 hour 24 minutes.
So the next bus is at 9:24 am.

misconceptions.A: This is not one of the bus times. List them from 7:00 am, adding 36 minutes each time.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The bus before leaves at 8:48 am, and 36 minutes later is 9:24 am.
misconceptions.C: Check your list of bus times. After 8:48 am, add 36 minutes to find the next one.
misconceptions.D: This is too late. A bus leaves at 8:48 am, and the next one is only 36 minutes after that.

questionText: If it takes 10 seconds to print a picture, how many pictures can be printed in half an hour?
hints: The two times are in different units. Change them to the same unit before you divide.
Half an hour is 30 minutes. Find how many pictures are printed in 1 minute first.
Similar example: a machine takes 15 seconds to fill a bottle. In 1 minute it fills 60 ÷ 15 = 4 bottles. In a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes, it fills 15 × 4 = 60 bottles.

stepByStep.text: Find the pictures printed in 1 minute, which is 60 seconds.
Half an hour is 30 minutes.
Multiply the pictures per minute by 30. So 180 pictures can be printed.

misconceptions.A: 30 is the number of minutes in half an hour. In each of those minutes 6 pictures are printed.
misconceptions.B: This multiplies 60 by 10. Divide instead: 60 ÷ 10 gives 6 pictures a minute, then multiply by 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 6 pictures a minute for 30 minutes makes 6 × 30 = 180.
misconceptions.D: This is 30 × 10. Each minute gives 6 pictures, so multiply 30 by 6.

questionText: A bell rings after every 35 minutes. If it rang for the first time at 9:00 am, when will it ring for the 5th time?
hints: Count the gaps between rings, not the rings. The first ring happens at the start, before any gap has passed.
From the 1st ring to the 5th ring there are 4 gaps. Find how many minutes 4 gaps of 35 minutes make.
Similar example: a bell rings every 25 minutes, first at 8:00 am. The 4th ring comes after 3 gaps: 3 × 25 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. So it rings for the 4th time at 9:15 am.

stepByStep.text: From the 1st ring to the 5th ring there are 4 gaps.
Find the time for 4 gaps.
140 minutes is 2 hours 20 minutes.
2 hours 20 minutes after 9:00 am is 11:20 am.

misconceptions.A: Yes! 4 gaps of 35 minutes make 140 minutes, which is 2 hours 20 minutes after 9:00 am.
misconceptions.B: Write the ring times: 9:00, 9:35, 10:10, 10:45 and then the 5th. Each is 35 minutes after the one before.
misconceptions.C: Check the ring times one by one. Add 35 minutes four times, starting from 9:00 am.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 gaps of 35 minutes. From the 1st ring to the 5th there are only 4 gaps.

questionText: A train left Pune at quarter past eight in the morning and reached Mumbai at quarter to 1 in the afternoon. If the actual duration is 3 hours 40 min, by how many minutes was the train late?
hints: First find how long the journey really took. Then compare it with how long it should take.
Write the times as clock times: quarter past eight is 8:15 am and quarter to 1 is 12:45 pm. Find the time between them.

Similar example: a bus leaves at quarter past nine and arrives at half past twelve. From 9:15 to 12:15 is 3 hours, and 15 minutes more makes 3 hours 15 minutes. If the trip should take 2 hours 45 minutes, the bus is 30 minutes late.

stepByStep.text: Quarter past eight is 8:15 am. Quarter to 1 is 12:45 pm.
From 8:15 am to 12:15 pm is 4 hours. Then 30 minutes more takes us to 12:45 pm. The journey took 4 hours 30 minutes.
Change to minutes. 4 hours 30 minutes is 270 minutes.
The journey should take 3 hours 40 minutes, which is 220 minutes.
Subtract. The train was late by 50 min.

misconceptions.A: Check the journey time. From 8:15 am to 12:45 pm is 4 hours 30 minutes. Then take away 3 hours 40 minutes.
misconceptions.B: Check the subtraction. 4 hours 30 minutes is 270 minutes and 3 hours 40 minutes is 220 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The journey took 270 minutes instead of 220 minutes, and 270 − 220 = 50.
misconceptions.D: Quarter to 1 means 15 minutes before 1 o'clock, which is 12:45. Find the journey time from 8:15 to 12:45.

questionText: Priya's watch is 10 minutes slow and Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast. If Kriya's watch is 3:45 pm, what is the time in Priya's watch?
hints: A fast watch shows a later time than the real time. A slow watch shows an earlier time. Find the real time first.
Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast, so the real time is 5 minutes before 3:45 pm. Work that out first.
Similar example: Ravi's watch is 10 minutes fast and shows 6:20. So the real time is 6:10. Meena's watch is 15 minutes slow, so it shows 15 minutes before 6:10, which is 5:55.

stepByStep.text: Kriya's watch is 5 minutes fast. So the real time is 5 minutes before 3:45 pm, which is 3:40 pm.
Priya's watch is 10 minutes slow. So it shows 10 minutes before the real time.
Take 10 minutes from 3:40 pm. Priya's watch shows 3:30 pm.

misconceptions.A: This adds both amounts. A fast watch is ahead, so go back 5 minutes for the real time, then back 10 more for the slow watch.
misconceptions.B: This is the real time. Priya's watch is 10 minutes behind it.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The real time is 3:40 pm, and a watch that is 10 minutes slow shows 3:30 pm.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 minutes. Kriya's watch is fast, so the real time is earlier than 3:45 pm.

questionText: A clock loses 10 minutes every hour. It was set correctly at 1:00 am. What time will this clock show when the actual time is 6:00 am?
hints: A clock that loses time falls further behind every hour. Find how many hours pass, then how much time is lost in total.
Count the hours from 1:00 am to 6:00 am. The clock loses 10 minutes in each of those hours.
Similar example: a clock loses 6 minutes every hour and is set right at 2:00 pm. At 7:00 pm, 5 hours have passed. It has lost 5 × 6 = 30 minutes, so it shows 6:30 pm.

stepByStep.text: Count the hours from 1:00 am to 6:00 am.
The clock loses 10 minutes in each hour.
The clock is 50 minutes behind 6:00 am. So it shows 5:10 am.

misconceptions.A: This adds the 50 minutes. A clock that loses time is behind, so go back 50 minutes from 6:00 am.
misconceptions.B: Yes! In 5 hours the clock loses 50 minutes, and 50 minutes before 6:00 am is 5:10 am.
misconceptions.C: This is only 10 minutes behind. The clock loses 10 minutes in each of the 5 hours.
misconceptions.D: This is 60 minutes behind. Only 5 hours pass, so the clock loses 5 × 10 = 50 minutes.

questionText: A watch gains 5 min every hour. It was set correctly at noon. What is the actual time when this watch shows quarter past three?
hints: A watch that gains time runs ahead. In one real hour it moves forward more than 60 minutes. Think about how far the watch moves in each real hour.
In 1 real hour this watch moves 65 minutes. From noon to quarter past three the watch has moved 3 hours 15 minutes. Change that to minutes.

Similar example: a watch gains 10 minutes every hour and is set right at noon. In each real hour it moves 70 minutes. When it shows 2:20 pm it has moved 140 minutes, and 140 ÷ 70 = 2. So 2 real hours have passed and the real time is 2:00 pm.

stepByStep.text: In 1 real hour the watch moves 5 minutes extra.
From noon to quarter past three, the watch has moved 3 hours 15 minutes.
See how many lots of 65 minutes fit in 195 minutes.
So 3 real hours have passed since noon. The actual time is 3:00 pm.

misconceptions.A: Yes! In 3 real hours the watch gains 15 minutes, so it shows 3:15 pm when the real time is 3:00 pm.
misconceptions.B: This takes off only 5 minutes. The watch gains 5 minutes in every hour, and 3 hours have passed.
misconceptions.C: This takes off 30 minutes. In 3 real hours the watch gains 3 × 5 = 15 minutes.
misconceptions.D: This adds 5 minutes. A watch that gains time is ahead, so the real time is earlier than 3:15 pm.

questionText: How many leap years are there between 1990 and 2004?
hints: A leap year comes once every 4 years, and its number divides by 4 exactly. The word between means the two end years are not counted.
Find the first year after 1990 that divides by 4 exactly. Then keep adding 4, stopping before 2004.
Similar example: leap years between 2010 and 2030. The first is 2012, then 2016, 2020, 2024 and 2028. That makes 5 leap years.

stepByStep.text: 1990 does not divide by 4 exactly, but 1992 does.
Keep adding 4 years: 1992, 1996, 2000. The next one would be 2004.
2004 is an end year, so it is not between 1990 and 2004.
The leap years between them are 1992, 1996 and 2000. That is 3 leap years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The leap years between 1990 and 2004 are 1992, 1996 and 2000.
misconceptions.B: This also counts 2004. The word between leaves out the end years, so stop at 2000.
misconceptions.C: This counts too many. Leap years come once every 4 years: 1992, 1996 and 2000.
misconceptions.D: This counts every second year. Leap years come once every 4 years, starting here with 1992.

questionText: If the school vacation lasted from 17th April to 3rd June, how long was the vacation?
hints: Count the days month by month: the days left in April, all of May, and the days in June. Remember how many days each month has.
April has 30 days. Count the vacation days in April from the 17th to the 30th, and include the 17th itself.
Similar example: a camp runs from 20th June to 5th July. June has 30 days, so June gives 30 − 20 + 1 = 11 days. July gives 5 days. The camp lasts 11 + 5 = 16 days.

stepByStep.text: April has 30 days. From the 17th to the 30th, counting the 17th too, there are 14 days.
May has 31 days.
June gives 3 days, from the 1st to the 3rd.
Add the three parts. The vacation was 48 days.

misconceptions.A: Check the days in each month. April gives 14 days, May gives 31 and June gives 3.
misconceptions.B: This leaves out the first day. The 17th of April is part of the vacation, so April gives 14 days, not 13.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 14 days in April, 31 in May and 3 in June make 14 + 31 + 3 = 48.
misconceptions.D: This is one day too many. Check that May has 31 days and June gives just 3.

questionText: The school vacation began on 22nd April and lasted for 40 days. When did the school reopen?
hints: Count the vacation days month by month. The school reopens on the day after the last vacation day.
April has 30 days. Count the vacation days in April from the 22nd to the 30th, including the 22nd. Then see how many of the 40 days are left for May.

Similar example: a holiday begins on 25th June and lasts 20 days. June has 30 days, so June gives 30 − 25 + 1 = 6 days. That leaves 20 − 6 = 14 days in July, so the last holiday is 14th July. School reopens on 15th July.

stepByStep.text: April gives the days from the 22nd to the 30th, counting the 22nd too.
Find how many vacation days are left after April.
May has exactly 31 days, so the last day of the vacation is 31st May.
The school reopens the next day, on 1st June.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The 40 days end on 31st May, so school reopens the next day.
misconceptions.B: 31st May is the last day of the vacation. School reopens the day after.
misconceptions.C: This is one day late. Count 22nd April as the first vacation day, so April gives 9 days.
misconceptions.D: This goes backwards from April. The vacation moves forward 40 days, through May.

questionText: A train leaves Pune station at 17:20 on the 24-hour clock. What is this time on the 12-hour clock?
hints: On the 24-hour clock, hours bigger than 12 are afternoon or evening times.
Take 12 away from the hours: 17 - 12. The minutes stay the same.
Example: 14:35 on the 24-hour clock. 14 - 12 = 2, so it is 2:35 pm.

stepByStep.text: 17 is more than 12, so the time is after noon and is a pm time.
Take 12 away from the hours.
The minutes stay as 20, so the time is 5:20 pm.

misconceptions.A: That is right! 17 - 12 = 5, so 17:20 is 5:20 pm.
misconceptions.B: This takes 10 away from 17. Noon is 12 o'clock, so take away 12.
misconceptions.C: The hour 5 is right, but 17:20 comes after noon, so it is pm.
misconceptions.D: This takes 13 away from 17. Noon is 12 o'clock, so take away 12.

questionText: How many days are there altogether in the months of June and July?
hints: You need to remember how many days each month has. The knuckle trick or the rhyme 'Thirty days has September' can help.
June has 30 days. How many days does July have?
Example: December has 31 days and January has 31 days. Together they have 31 + 31 = 62 days.

stepByStep.text: June has 30 days.
July has 31 days.
Add them.
June and July have 61 days altogether.

misconceptions.A: This takes both months as 30 days. July has 31 days.
misconceptions.B: Well done! 30 + 31 = 61.
misconceptions.C: This takes both months as 31 days. June has only 30 days.
misconceptions.D: This is too few. June has 30 days and July has 31 days.

questionText: How many days are there in February 2028?
hints: February is the only month whose length changes. It depends on whether the year is a leap year.
A year like this is a leap year if 4 divides it exactly. Try dividing 2028 by 4.
Example: For February 2023, divide 2023 by 4. It leaves a remainder of 3, so 2023 is not a leap year and its February has 28 days.

stepByStep.text: Check whether 4 divides 2028 exactly.
There is no remainder, so 2028 is a leap year.
In a leap year February has one extra day, so February 2028 has 29 days.

misconceptions.A: February has 28 days in an ordinary year. Check whether 2028 is a leap year by dividing it by 4.
misconceptions.B: February never has 30 days. It has 28 days, or one more in a leap year.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 2028 is a leap year, so February has 29 days.
misconceptions.D: February never has 31 days. It has 28 days, or one more in a leap year.

questionText: A film is 135 minutes long. How long is that in hours and minutes?
hints: One hour is 60 minutes. See how many full hours fit into the minutes, and what is left.
Two hours are 120 minutes. Is 135 more than 120? How much more?
Example: 80 minutes. One hour is 60 minutes, and 80 - 60 = 20, so 80 minutes is 1 hour 20 minutes.

stepByStep.text: Two full hours fit into 135 minutes.
Find the minutes left over.
135 minutes is 2 hours 15 minutes.

misconceptions.A: This reads 135 as 1 hour and 35 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, not 100.
misconceptions.B: The 2 hours are right, but 2 hours use up 120 minutes, leaving 15 minutes.
misconceptions.C: 3 hours would be 180 minutes, which is more than 135. Only 2 full hours fit.
misconceptions.D: Well done! 120 minutes make 2 hours, and 15 minutes are left.

questionText: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be 10 days from today?
hints: The days of the week repeat every 7 days. Take out the full weeks first.
7 days from Wednesday is Wednesday again. How many days are left out of 10 after taking away 7?
Example: Today is Monday. 9 days later: 7 days bring Monday again, and 2 more days give Wednesday.

stepByStep.text: After 7 days it is Wednesday again.
Days still to count.
Three days after Wednesday: Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
It will be Saturday.

misconceptions.A: That is right! 7 days bring Wednesday again, and 3 more days bring Saturday.
misconceptions.B: This counts Wednesday itself as the first day. Start counting from tomorrow, Thursday.
misconceptions.C: This counts one day too many. After the full week, only 3 more days are needed.
misconceptions.D: Wednesday comes again after 7 days. There are 3 more days to count after that.

questionText: Arjun's school starts at 8:00 am and ends at 1:30 pm. How long is his school day?
hints: The time passes 12 noon, so count in two parts: up to noon, and after noon.
Find how long it is from 8:00 am to 12 noon.
Example: From 9:00 am to 2:15 pm. From 9:00 am to noon is 3 hours, and from noon to 2:15 pm is 2 hours 15 minutes, so 5 hours 15 minutes in all.

stepByStep.text: From 8:00 am to 12 noon.
From 12 noon to 1:30 pm is 1 hour 30 minutes.
4 hours and 1 hour 30 minutes make 5 hours 30 minutes.

misconceptions.A: This subtracts 1 from 8. The clock passes 12 noon, so count up to noon and then on to 1:30 pm.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 4 hours before noon and 1 hour 30 minutes after noon make 5 hours 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: This counts one hour too many. From 8:00 am to noon is 4 hours, then add 1 hour 30 minutes.
misconceptions.D: This leaves out an hour. From 8:00 am to noon is 4 hours, then add 1 hour 30 minutes.

questionText: Dadi's favourite TV serial starts at a quarter to 7 in the evening. What is this time on the 24-hour clock?
hints: First write the time with hours and minutes, then change it to the 24-hour clock.
A quarter to 7 means 15 minutes before 7 o'clock. Which hour is it still in, and how many minutes past?
Example: A quarter to 4 in the afternoon is 3:45 pm. Adding 12 to the hours gives 15:45.

stepByStep.text: A quarter to 7 is 15 minutes before 7 o'clock, which is 6:45.
It is evening, so the time is 6:45 pm.
For a pm time, add 12 to the hours.
On the 24-hour clock the time is 18:45.

misconceptions.A: This is a quarter past 7 in the evening. A quarter to 7 is 15 minutes before 7 o'clock.
misconceptions.B: 6:45 is right, but this is the morning time. For the evening, add 12 to the hours.
misconceptions.C: Well done! A quarter to 7 in the evening is 6:45 pm, which is 18:45.
misconceptions.D: This puts 45 minutes after 7 o'clock. A quarter to 7 is before 7, in the hour of 6.

questionText: A train journey from Kanyakumari to Jammu takes exactly 3 days. How many hours is that?
hints: Think about how many hours make one full day, counting day and night together.
One day has 24 hours. Find 3 lots of 24.
Example: 2 days are 2 x 24 = 48 hours.

stepByStep.text: One full day has 24 hours.
Multiply by 3 days.
The journey takes 72 hours.

misconceptions.A: This uses 12 hours for a day. A full day, with its night, has 24 hours.
misconceptions.B: This multiplies by 60. There are 60 minutes in an hour, but 24 hours in a day.
misconceptions.C: This adds 3 and 24. Three days are 3 lots of 24 hours, so multiply.
misconceptions.D: That is right! 3 x 24 = 72 hours.

questionText: A night bus leaves Bengaluru at 9:30 pm. The journey to Chennai takes 6 hours 45 minutes. At what time does the bus reach Chennai?
hints: The journey crosses midnight, so the answer will be an am time on the next day. Add the hours and the minutes in parts.
Add the 6 hours first. Going 6 hours on from 9:30 pm passes midnight: where do you land?
Example: Leave at 10:40 pm and travel 3 hours 30 minutes. Three hours later it is 1:40 am, and 30 more minutes make 2:10 am.

stepByStep.text: Add 6 hours to 9:30 pm: it becomes 3:30 am the next day.
Now add 45 minutes. 30 minutes take the time to 4:00 am.
The remaining minutes.
The bus reaches Chennai at 4:15 am.

misconceptions.A: The 75 minutes from 30 + 45 make 1 hour and 15 minutes. Carry that extra hour to the hours.
misconceptions.B: Well done! 6 hours later is 3:30 am, and 45 minutes more is 4:15 am.
misconceptions.C: The numbers are right, but the bus travels through the night, so it arrives in the early morning, am.
misconceptions.D: This goes back 6 hours 45 minutes. The journey time must be added to the starting time.

questionText: A train leaves Mumbai at 22:40 and reaches Goa at 05:10 the next morning. How long is the journey?
hints: The journey crosses midnight. Split it into the part before midnight and the part after midnight.
Find how long it is from 22:40 to midnight, which is 24:00.
Example: From 23:15 to 02:30 the next day. Up to midnight is 45 minutes, and after midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes, so 3 hours 15 minutes in all.

stepByStep.text: From 22:40 to midnight is 1 hour 20 minutes.
From midnight to 05:10 is 5 hours 10 minutes.
Add: 1 hour 20 minutes and 5 hours 10 minutes make 6 hours 30 minutes.
The journey takes 6 hours 30 minutes.

misconceptions.A: This subtracts 05:10 from 22:40. The train arrives the next day, so count on through midnight.
misconceptions.B: This is one hour too long. From 22:40 to midnight is only 1 hour 20 minutes.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 1 hour 20 minutes before midnight and 5 hours 10 minutes after make 6 hours 30 minutes.
misconceptions.D: This adds 40 minutes and 10 minutes. Before midnight there are only 20 minutes left in the hour after 22:40.

questionText: In a certain month, the 5th is a Tuesday. What day of the week is the 23rd of the same month?
hints: The same day of the week comes again every 7 days. Jump forward in sevens from the date you know.
Add 7 to the 5th again and again to find other Tuesdays: 5, 12, and so on.
Example: The 3rd is a Monday. The 10th and 17th are also Mondays, so the 20th, three days later, is a Thursday.

stepByStep.text: The Tuesdays are 7 days apart.
So the 19th is a Tuesday.
Days from the 19th to the 23rd.
Four days after Tuesday: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
The 23rd is a Saturday.

misconceptions.A: This stops one day early. From Tuesday the 19th, count 4 days on to reach the 23rd.
misconceptions.B: This goes one day too far. From Tuesday the 19th, count 4 days on to reach the 23rd.
misconceptions.C: This counts only 2 days on from the 19th. The 23rd is 4 days after the 19th.
misconceptions.D: That is right! The 19th is a Tuesday, and 4 days later is Saturday.

questionText: How many days after 20 February 2024 is 5 March 2024?
hints: Count the days left in February, then the days in March. Check how long February is in that year.
2024 can be divided exactly by 4, so it is a leap year. How many days does its February have?
Example: From 25 February 2023 to 4 March 2023. February 2023 has 28 days, so 3 days are left in February, and 4 more in March make 7 days.

stepByStep.text: 2024 is a leap year, so February has 29 days.
Days left in February after the 20th.
Add the 5 days of March.
5 March 2024 is 14 days after 20 February 2024.

misconceptions.A: Well done! 9 days are left in February 2024, and 5 days of March make 14.
misconceptions.B: This takes February as 28 days. 2024 is a leap year, so its February has 29 days.
misconceptions.C: This takes February as 30 days. In the leap year 2024, February has 29 days.
misconceptions.D: This takes February as 31 days. In the leap year 2024, February has 29 days.

questionText: Anil practises the tabla for 40 minutes every day. For how long does he practise in one week?
hints: Find the total minutes for the week, then change the minutes into hours and minutes.
A week has 7 days. Find 7 lots of 40 minutes.
Example: 50 minutes a day for 3 days is 150 minutes. Two hours are 120 minutes, so that is 2 hours 30 minutes.

stepByStep.text: Minutes in one week.
Four hours are 240 minutes.
Minutes left over.
He practises for 4 hours 40 minutes in one week.

misconceptions.A: This counts only 5 days. Anil practises every day, and a week has 7 days.
misconceptions.B: Yes! 280 minutes is 4 hours 40 minutes.
misconceptions.C: This reads 280 as 2 hours and 80 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so 280 minutes hold 4 full hours.
misconceptions.D: The 4 hours are right. Check the minutes left: 280 - 240.

questionText: A month has 30 days, and its 1st day is a Saturday. How many Sundays are there in this month?
hints: Find the date of the first Sunday, then keep jumping forward 7 days until the month ends.
If the 1st is a Saturday, the first Sunday is the very next day, the 2nd.
Example: A month of 30 days begins on a Monday. Its first Sunday is the 7th, and the others are the 14th, 21st and 28th, so that month has 4 Sundays.

stepByStep.text: The 1st is a Saturday, so the 2nd is the first Sunday.
Add 7 each time: the Sundays are the 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th.
The 30th is still inside the month.
There are 5 Sundays in this month.

misconceptions.A: 30 days hold 4 full weeks and 2 extra days. The extra days here are a Saturday and a Sunday, so there is one more Sunday.
misconceptions.B: A sixth Sunday would be on the 37th, and the month has only 30 days.
misconceptions.C: Great counting! The Sundays are the 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th.
misconceptions.D: Keep adding 7 until the month ends: 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30 are all Sundays.

questionText: Kavya's train leaves at 14:10. She wants to reach the station 25 minutes before the train leaves, and it takes her 35 minutes to travel from home to the station. What is the latest time she can leave home?
hints: Work backwards from the train time. Both the early arrival and the travel time come before the train leaves.
Add the two amounts of time she needs before 14:10: 25 minutes and 35 minutes.
Example: A bus leaves at 16:30. Rahul wants to be 10 minutes early and needs 20 minutes to get there. He needs 30 minutes in all, so he leaves at 16:00, which is 4:00 pm.

stepByStep.text: Total time needed before the train leaves.
60 minutes is 1 hour.
One hour before 14:10 is 13:10.
Change to the 12-hour clock.
The latest she can leave home is 1:10 pm.

misconceptions.A: This is the time she wants to reach the station. She must leave home 35 minutes before that.
misconceptions.B: This takes away only the 35 minutes of travel. She also wants to be 25 minutes early.
misconceptions.C: This goes forward from the train time. She has to leave home before the train, so count backwards.
misconceptions.D: Well done! She needs 60 minutes in all, and one hour before 14:10 is 1:10 pm.

questionText: In the year 2016 Republic day was on Tuesday. In which year would Republic Day fall on a Sunday?
hints: A date moves forward by 1 day of the week after an ordinary year, because 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day. It moves forward by 2 days when a 29 February falls in between.
Republic Day is 26 January. 2016 is a leap year, and its 29 February comes after Republic Day. So first work out the day for 26 January 2017, then go on year by year.

Here is a similar one. 15 August 2010 was a Sunday. An ordinary year pushes the day on by 1, so 15 August 2011 was a Monday. Between 15 August 2011 and 15 August 2012 there is a 29 February, so the day moves on by 2, to Wednesday.

stepByStep.text: Republic Day is 26 January. A year of 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day of the week moves on by 1. If a 29 February falls in between, it moves on by 2.
2016 is a leap year and its 29 February comes after 26 January. So from 2016 to 2017 the day moves on by 2: Tuesday becomes Thursday. This is the step that is easy to miss.
From 2017 to 2018 the day moves on by 1 to Friday, and from 2018 to 2019 it moves on by 1 to Saturday.
From 26 January 2019 to 26 January 2020 there is no 29 February in between, because the leap day of 2020 comes later. The day moves on by 1 to Sunday.
So Republic Day falls on a Sunday in 2020.

misconceptions.A: Excellent thinking! The day moves from Tuesday to Thursday, Friday, Saturday and then Sunday, which is in 2020.
misconceptions.B: In 2019 Republic Day was on a Saturday. Count again from 2016, and remember that the leap day of 2016 pushes 2017 on by 2 days.
misconceptions.C: In 2021 Republic Day was on a Tuesday, because the leap day of 2020 falls before 26 January 2021. Sunday comes one year earlier.
misconceptions.D: In 2022 Republic Day was on a Wednesday. Count on from Tuesday in 2016 one year at a time, adding 2 days when a 29 February is passed.

questionText: All Fool's Day in 2017 was on Saturday, Then on what day will the Teachers Day fall on in the same year?
hints: All Fool's Day is 1 April and Teachers' Day is 5 September. Count the days from one to the other, then see how many are left over after full weeks.
Count the days left in April after the 1st, then all of May, June, July and August, then the 5 days of September. Remember which months have 30 days and which have 31.

Here is a similar one. If 1 March is a Monday, what day is 10 April? There are 30 more days in March and 10 in April, which is 40 days. 40 days is 5 weeks and 5 days, and 5 days after Monday is Saturday.

stepByStep.text: Teachers' Day is 5 September. Count the days after 1 April: 29 more in April, 31 in May, 30 in June, 31 in July, 31 in August and 5 in September.
Add them up to get 157 days.
Every 7 days brings back the same day of the week. 22 weeks is 22 × 7 = 154 days, so 157 days is 22 weeks and 3 days.
Three days after Saturday is Tuesday. Teachers' Day fell on a Tuesday.

misconceptions.A: Monday is 2 days after Saturday. Count the days once more: after the full weeks are taken out, 3 days should be left over.
misconceptions.B: Sunday is only 1 day after Saturday. Check the month lengths: May, July and August have 31 days each.
misconceptions.C: Friday would be 6 days after Saturday. Add the days from 1 April to 5 September again and take out the full weeks.
misconceptions.D: You got it! There are 157 days from 1 April to 5 September, which is 22 weeks and 3 days, and 3 days after Saturday is Tuesday.

questionText: The movement of the minute hand in which of the following is 50 minutes?
hints: On a clock face, the minute hand takes 5 minutes to move from one number to the next. Count the steps the hand moves, always going forward the way a clock turns.
Work out how many 5-minute steps make 50 minutes. Then count the steps for each choice, going forward past XII where you need to.
Here is a similar one. How long does the minute hand take to go from VIII to II? Going forward, it passes IX, X, XI, XII, I and II, which is 6 steps. 6 × 5 = 30, so it takes 30 minutes.

stepByStep.text: The minute hand takes 5 minutes to go from one number to the next. So 50 minutes is 10 steps.
From IX forward to III, the hand passes 12 and moves 6 steps, which is 30 minutes. From X to VI is 8 steps and from IV to XII is 8 steps, which is 40 minutes each.
From VI, the hand moves 6 steps up to XII and then 4 more steps on to IV. That is 10 steps.
10 steps of 5 minutes make 50 minutes. So the movement of 50 minutes is VI to IV.

misconceptions.A: From IX forward to III is 6 steps, which is 30 minutes. Look for a move of 10 steps.
misconceptions.B: From X forward to VI is 8 steps, which is 40 minutes. Look for a move of 10 steps.
misconceptions.C: From IV forward to XII is 8 steps, which is 40 minutes. Look for a move of 10 steps.
misconceptions.D: Well done! From VI the hand moves forward 10 steps to reach IV, and 10 steps of 5 minutes make 50 minutes.

questionText: A watch gains 2 minutes every hour. If it is set correctly at 8:00 a.m., then what will be the time in this watch at 8:00 p.m the same day?
hints: A watch that gains runs a little ahead of the real time. Find how much it gains altogether, then decide whether to add that or take it away.
Count the hours from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. The watch gains 2 minutes in each of those hours.
Here is a similar one. A clock gains 3 minutes every hour and is set right at 6:00 a.m. By 11:00 a.m., 5 hours have passed, so it has gained 5 × 3 = 15 minutes. It shows 11:15 a.m.

stepByStep.text: From 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 12 hours.
The watch gains 2 minutes in every hour, so in 12 hours it gains 24 minutes.
A watch that gains is ahead of the real time, so the 24 minutes are added. Taking them away is the trap here.
24 minutes after 8:00 p.m. is 8:24 p.m. The watch shows 8:24 p.m.

misconceptions.A: 8:20 p.m. is a gain of 20 minutes, which is only 10 hours of gaining. From 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 12 hours.
misconceptions.B: 7:36 p.m. is 24 minutes behind the real time. A watch that gains runs ahead, so the 24 minutes are added.
misconceptions.C: Great job! The watch gains 2 minutes in each of 12 hours, which is 24 minutes, so it shows 8:24 p.m.
misconceptions.D: 8:02 p.m. is the gain for just 1 hour. The watch gains 2 minutes in each of the 12 hours.

questionText: A watch falls slow by 30 seconds in every hour. It is set to correct time at 8:00 a.m. What time would this watch show at 10 p.m. the same day
hints: A watch that runs slow falls a little behind the real time. Find how much it loses altogether, then decide whether to add that or take it away.
Count the hours from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The watch loses 30 seconds in each of those hours, so find the total in seconds and change it to minutes.
Here is a similar one. A clock loses 20 seconds every hour and is set right at 6:00 a.m. By 3:00 p.m., 9 hours have passed, so it has lost 9 × 20 = 180 seconds, which is 3 minutes. It shows 2:57 p.m.

stepByStep.text: From 8:00 a.m. to noon is 4 hours, and from noon to 10:00 p.m. is 10 hours. That is 14 hours.
The watch loses 30 seconds in each hour, so in 14 hours it loses 420 seconds.
Change the seconds to minutes. 420 seconds is 7 minutes.
A slow watch is behind the real time, so the 7 minutes are taken away, not added. 7 minutes before 10:00 p.m. is 9:53 p.m., so the watch shows 9:53 p.m.

misconceptions.A: 9:57 p.m. is only 3 minutes behind. Count the hours from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. again: there are 14, and each one loses half a minute.
misconceptions.B: 9:46 p.m. is 14 minutes behind, which would be a whole minute lost every hour. The watch loses only 30 seconds an hour, which is half a minute.
misconceptions.C: Excellent thinking! In 14 hours the watch loses 7 minutes, so it shows 9:53 p.m.
misconceptions.D: 10:07 p.m. is 7 minutes ahead. A slow watch falls behind, so the 7 minutes are taken away.

questionText: Express the time 3 hrs 45 min as decimal fraction
hints: A decimal shows parts out of 10 or 100, but minutes are parts out of 60. Work out what fraction of an hour the minutes make before you write a decimal.
Keep the 3 whole hours as they are. Write 45 minutes as a fraction of 60 minutes and make that fraction as simple as you can.
Here is a similar one. Write 2 hours 30 minutes as a decimal. 30 minutes out of 60 is 30/60, which is 1/2 of an hour, or 0.5 of an hour. So it is 2.5 hours.

stepByStep.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 45 minutes is 45/60 of an hour.
Make the fraction simpler by dividing the top and the bottom by 15. 45/60 is the same as 3/4.
3/4 is the same as 75/100, which is 0.75 as a decimal.
Add this to the 3 whole hours. 3 hrs 45 min is 3.75 hr.

misconceptions.A: 0.15 of an hour is only 9 minutes. 45 minutes is three quarters of an hour, so find the decimal for three quarters.
misconceptions.B: 3.45 just copies the minutes after the point. Minutes are parts of 60, not parts of 100, so 45 minutes is 45/60 of an hour.
misconceptions.C: You got it! 45 minutes is 3/4 of an hour, which is 0.75, so the time is 3.75 hr.
misconceptions.D: 0.045 of an hour is less than 3 minutes. Write 45 minutes as 45/60 of an hour and make the fraction simpler.

questionText: 1st of January 2006 fell on a Sunday. Then on which day did 1st January 2010 fall on?
hints: A date moves forward by 1 day of the week after an ordinary year, because 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day. After a leap year of 366 days it moves forward by 2 days.
List the four years that pass: 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009. Decide which of them is a leap year by checking which one divides exactly by 4.

Here is a similar one. 1 January 2014 was a Wednesday. 2014 and 2015 are ordinary years, so 1 January 2015 was a Thursday and 1 January 2016 was a Friday. 2016 is a leap year, so the day moves on by 2, and 1 January 2017 was a Sunday.

stepByStep.text: An ordinary year has 365 days, which is 52 weeks and 1 day. So 1 January moves on by 1 day after an ordinary year and by 2 days after a leap year.
2006 and 2007 are ordinary years. So 1 January 2007 was a Monday and 1 January 2008 was a Tuesday.
2008 is a leap year, because it divides exactly by 4. So the day moves on by 2, and 1 January 2009 was a Thursday. This is the step that is easy to miss.
2009 is an ordinary year, so the day moves on by 1. 1st January 2010 fell on a Friday.

misconceptions.A: Saturday is one day too far. Only one of the four years, 2008, is a leap year, so the day moves on by 5 days in all.
misconceptions.B: Thursday counts 1 day for each of the four years. 2008 is a leap year, so it moves the day on by 2.
misconceptions.C: Monday is where 1 January 2007 fell, after just one year. Keep going for all four years.
misconceptions.D: Well done! Three ordinary years and one leap year move the day on by 5 days, from Sunday to Friday.

questionText: If 19th April 2018 was on Thursday, then which of the days appeared 5 times in that month?
hints: A month of 30 days is 4 full weeks and 2 extra days. Every day of the week comes 4 times, and the days that fall on the first two dates come a fifth time.
Go back from the 19th in steps of 7 to find a Thursday early in April. Then work out what day the 1st was.

Here is a similar one. Suppose 17 June is a Friday. Going back in 7s, 10 June and 3 June are Fridays too, so 1 June is a Wednesday. June has 30 days, so the days on the 1st and 2nd, Wednesday and Thursday, come 5 times.

stepByStep.text: Go back from Thursday 19 April in steps of 7. The 12th and the 5th of April are Thursdays too.
Count back from Thursday the 5th. The 4th is a Wednesday, the 3rd a Tuesday, the 2nd a Monday and the 1st a Sunday.
April has 30 days, which is 4 weeks and 2 days. The 29th and 30th fall on the same days as the 1st and 2nd.
Only the days of the 1st and 2nd come 5 times, and every other day comes 4 times. The days that appeared 5 times are Sunday & Monday.

misconceptions.A: Monday is right, but Tuesday is the 3rd, and April has no 31st to give it a fifth turn. Check what day the 1st was.
misconceptions.B: Only 2 days can come 5 times in a month of 30 days. Thursday falls on the 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th, which is just 4 times.
misconceptions.C: Sunday is right, but Saturday falls on the 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th, which is only 4 times. The extra days are the 29th and 30th.
misconceptions.D: Great job! 1 April was a Sunday, so Sunday and Monday also fall on the 29th and 30th and come 5 times.

questionText: A boy celebrated his 10th birthday on 15th April 2019 which was a Monday. His 12th birthday will fall on which day of the week?
hints: The 12th birthday is two years after the 10th. Each ordinary year moves the day forward by 1, and a 29th February in between moves it by 2.
Go from 15th April 2019 to 15th April 2020 first. Check whether 29th February 2020 falls in between.

Similar example: a girl turns 8 on 10th May 2015, a Sunday. From May 2015 to May 2016 we pass 29th February 2016, so her 9th birthday is 2 days on, a Tuesday. The next year is ordinary, so her 10th birthday is a Wednesday.

stepByStep.text: The 12th birthday is on 15th April 2021, two years later.
From April 2019 to April 2020 we pass 29th February 2020. So the day moves on by 2, from Monday to Wednesday.
From April 2020 to April 2021 there is no leap day. So the day moves on by 1, from Wednesday to Thursday.
The 12th birthday falls on a Thursday.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The day moves 2 days in the first year and 1 day in the second, from Monday to Thursday.
misconceptions.B: This moves only 1 day. Two years pass, and one of them includes 29th February 2020.
misconceptions.C: That is the day of the 11th birthday. One more year moves it on again.
misconceptions.D: This goes backwards. Days move forward each year: 2 days in the first year and 1 in the second.

questionText: Which of the following is a leap year?
hints: A leap year is a year that divides exactly by 4. Years that end in 00 are special: they are leap years only if they divide exactly by 400.
Sort the four years into two groups: those that end in 00 and those that do not. Test the 00 years with 400 and the others with 4.

Here is a similar one. Is 2016 a leap year? 2016 ÷ 4 = 504 with nothing left over, and it does not end in 00, so 2016 is a leap year. But 1800 ends in 00 and does not divide exactly by 400, so 1800 is not a leap year.

stepByStep.text: A year is a leap year if it divides exactly by 4. Years ending in 00 must divide exactly by 400 instead.
2023 is an odd number, so it does not divide exactly by 4. It is not a leap year.
2100 and 1900 end in 00, and neither divides exactly by 400. So they are not leap years, even though they divide by 4. This is the trap.
2024 divides exactly by 4 and does not end in 00. So the leap year is 2024.

misconceptions.A: 2100 divides by 4, but it ends in 00, so it must divide exactly by 400. It does not, so 2100 is not a leap year.
misconceptions.B: 1900 divides by 4, but it ends in 00, so it must divide exactly by 400. It does not, so 1900 is not a leap year.
misconceptions.C: Excellent thinking! 2024 ÷ 4 = 506 exactly, and it does not end in 00, so 2024 is a leap year.
misconceptions.D: 2023 is an odd number, so it cannot be divided exactly by 4. Look for a year that divides by 4.

questionText: How many days are there from 1st March to 1st May (including both dates)?
hints: Count the days month by month. Remember how many days each month has, and notice that both the first date and the last date are to be counted.
Start with March: count every day from the 1st to the 31st. Then think about how many days April has, and what is still left to count after April.
Here is a similar one. How many days are there from 1 April to 10 May, counting both dates? April has 30 days, and then there are 10 days in May. 30 + 10 = 40, so there are 40 days.

stepByStep.text: Count all of March. From the 1st to the 31st is 31 days.
Count all of April, which has 30 days.
Then count 1 May itself, because both dates are included. That is 1 more day.
Add the three parts. There are 62 days.

misconceptions.A: 61 counts March and April but leaves out 1 May. Both dates are included, so add 1 more day.
misconceptions.B: You got it! 31 days in March, 30 in April and 1 day in May make 62 days.
misconceptions.C: 63 is one too many. March has 31 days and April has 30, and then comes just 1 day in May.
misconceptions.D: 60 treats both months as 30 days and leaves out 1 May. March has 31 days, and 1 May is counted too.

questionText: If 1st January 2023 was a Sunday, what day was 1st January 2024?
hints: From 1 January of one year to 1 January of the next is one whole year. Find how many days that is, then see how many are left over after full weeks.
Decide whether 2023 is a leap year by checking if it divides exactly by 4. That tells you how many days pass.
Here is a similar one. 1 January 2021 was a Friday. 2021 is not a leap year, so 365 days pass, which is 52 weeks and 1 day. The day moves on by 1, so 1 January 2022 was a Saturday.

stepByStep.text: From 1 January 2023 to 1 January 2024 is the whole of 2023. 2023 is not a leap year, so that is 365 days.
52 weeks is 52 × 7 = 364 days. So 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day.
After 52 full weeks it is Sunday again. One more day makes it Monday, so 1st January 2024 was a Monday.

misconceptions.A: It would be Sunday again only if a year were exactly 52 weeks, which is 364 days. 2023 has 365 days, so there is 1 day extra.
misconceptions.B: Saturday is one day back. The extra day moves the date forward, not backward.
misconceptions.C: Tuesday is a move of 2 days, which happens when 366 days pass. The days being counted here are all in 2023, which has 365 days.
misconceptions.D: Well done! 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves on from Sunday to Monday.

questionText: If 1st January 2024 was a Monday, what day was 1st January 2025?

stepByStep.text: 2024 is a leap year: 366 days.
2 extra days: Monday + 2 = Wednesday
1st January 2025 is Wednesday.

questionText: In 2007, Republic Day fell on Friday. On what day was it celebrated in 2008?
hints: Count the days from one Republic Day to the next, then see how many are left over after full weeks. Check whether a 29 February falls between the two dates.

Here is a similar one. 15 August 2013 was a Thursday. No 29 February lies between that day and 15 August 2014, so 365 days pass. That is 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves on by 1, to Friday.

stepByStep.text: Republic Day is 26 January. Between 26 January 2007 and 26 January 2008 there is no 29 February, because the leap day of 2008 comes later, in February.
So 365 days pass. 52 weeks is 364 days, so that is 52 weeks and 1 day.
The day moves on by 1, from Friday to Saturday. In 2008, Republic Day was celebrated on a Saturday.

misconceptions.A: Thursday is one day back. The extra day in 365 days moves the date forward, not backward.
misconceptions.B: Great job! 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day, so Republic Day moves on from Friday to Saturday.
misconceptions.C: It would be Friday again only if exactly 52 weeks, or 364 days, had passed. There are 365 days between the two dates.
misconceptions.D: Sunday is a move of 2 days. 2008 is a leap year, but its extra day comes on 29 February, after Republic Day, so only 1 day is added.

questionText: If 14th February 1992 was a Friday, what day did 13th February 1993 fall on?
hints: 1992 is a leap year! From 14 Feb 1992 to 14 Feb 1993 = 366 days (crosses 29 Feb 1992).
366 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 2 days. So 14 Feb 1993 = Friday + 2 = Sunday.
But we want 13 Feb (one day BEFORE 14 Feb). Sunday − 1 = Saturday.

stepByStep.text: 1992 is a leap year. 14 Feb 1992 to 14 Feb 1993 = 366 days.
14 Feb 1993 = Friday + 2 = Sunday
13 Feb 1993 = Sunday − 1 = Saturday
13 Feb 1993 was Saturday.

misconceptions.A: Got 14 Feb 1993 = Sunday but forgot to go back 1 day to 13th
misconceptions.C: Forgot leap year (only advanced 1 day) and went back 1
misconceptions.D: Assumed same day after 1 year

questionText: In a certain year, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday occurred 5 times each in the month of July. Which date fell on a Sunday?
questionLatex: \text{July: Wed, Thu, Fri occur 5 times. Which date is Sunday?}
hints: A month of 31 days is 4 full weeks and 3 extra days. The days that come 5 times are the days that fall on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd.
Wednesday, Thursday and Friday come 5 times, so decide which of them falls on 1 July. Then count forward to the first Sunday.

Here is a similar one. In a month of 30 days, Monday and Tuesday come 5 times. The two extra days, the 29th and 30th, match the 1st and 2nd, so the 1st is a Monday. The first Sunday is then the 7th, and the other Sundays are the 14th, 21st and 28th.

stepByStep.text: July has 31 days, which is 4 weeks and 3 days. The three extra days, the 29th, 30th and 31st, fall on the same days as the 1st, 2nd and 3rd.
The days that come 5 times are Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. So 1 July is a Wednesday, 2 July a Thursday and 3 July a Friday. Seeing this is the key to the question.
Then 4 July is a Saturday and 5 July is the first Sunday.
Add 7 each time to find the other Sundays: the 12th, the 19th and the 26th. The date that fell on a Sunday is 26th July.

misconceptions.A: The 20th is the day after Sunday the 19th, so it is a Monday. Find the first Sunday and keep adding 7.
misconceptions.B: 1 July is a Wednesday, so the 8th and the 15th are Wednesdays too. Count on from the 1st to find the first Sunday.
misconceptions.C: Excellent thinking! 1 July is a Wednesday, so the Sundays are the 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th.
misconceptions.D: The 31st falls on the same day as the 3rd, which is a Friday. The Sundays are the 5th and every 7 days after it.

questionText: How many minutes are there in 3 hours 45 minutes?

questionText: A movie starts at 2:40 PM and ends at 5:10 PM. How long is the movie?
hints: To find how long something lasts, count up from the start time to the end time. Counting up in easy jumps is safer than subtracting.

Here is a similar one. A class starts at 9:50 AM and ends at 12:15 PM. From 9:50 to 10:00 is 10 minutes, from 10:00 to 12:00 is 2 hours, and from 12:00 to 12:15 is 15 minutes. That is 2 hours and 10 + 15 = 25 minutes.

stepByStep.text: Count up from 2:40 PM in easy jumps. From 2:40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes.
From 3:00 to 5:00 is 2 hours.
From 5:00 to 5:10 is 10 minutes.
Put the jumps together: 2 hours, and 20 minutes plus 10 minutes. The movie is 2 hours 30 minutes long.

misconceptions.A: 3 hours after 2:40 PM is 5:40 PM, which is already past the end of the movie. Count up to 3:00 first, then to 5:00, then to 5:10.
misconceptions.B: Well done! 20 minutes, then 2 hours, then 10 minutes make 2 hours 30 minutes.
misconceptions.C: 70 minutes is more than an hour, so this is really 3 hours 10 minutes, which is too long. Count up from 2:40 PM in jumps instead.
misconceptions.D: 2 hours 10 minutes after 2:40 PM is only 4:50 PM. There are 20 more minutes to go to reach 5:10 PM.

questionText: What is 3:45 PM in 24-hour format?

misconceptions.D: Great job! 3 + 12 = 15, and the minutes stay the same, so 3:45 PM is 15:45.

questionText: How many odd days are there in 400 years?
hints: Odd days are the days left over after you take out all the full weeks. Count the odd days that the ordinary years and the leap years give, then take out full weeks again.
An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2. First find how many leap years there are in 400 years, remembering that a year ending in 00 is a leap year only if it divides exactly by 400.

Here is a similar one. How many odd days are there in 5 years, if one of them is a leap year? The four ordinary years give 4 odd days and the leap year gives 2. 4 + 2 = 6, which is less than a full week, so there are 6 odd days.

stepByStep.text: An ordinary year is 52 weeks and 1 day, so it has 1 odd day. A leap year is 52 weeks and 2 days, so it has 2 odd days.
In 400 years, every 4th year makes 100 years. Three of the four years ending in 00 are not leap years, so there are 97 leap years and 303 ordinary years.
The ordinary years give 303 odd days and the leap years give 97 × 2 = 194 odd days. Together that is 497 days.
497 days is exactly 71 weeks, with nothing left over. So there are 0 odd days in 400 years.

misconceptions.A: 3 does not fit here. Count the leap years carefully, 97 of them in 400 years, then add up the odd days and take out full weeks of 7.
misconceptions.B: Excellent thinking! The 497 extra days make exactly 71 weeks, so there are 0 odd days left over.
misconceptions.C: 5 is the number of odd days in 100 years. In 400 years there is one more leap year than in four separate hundreds, and the total comes to full weeks exactly.
misconceptions.D: 1 is the number of odd days in a single ordinary year. Add up the odd days for all 400 years, then take out the full weeks.

questionText: In 2003, April Fools' Day (1st April) was on Tuesday. On which day was it celebrated in 2004?

Here is a similar problem. 15th August 2015 was a Saturday. Between 15th August 2015 and 15th August 2016 there is a 29th of February, because 2016 is a leap year, so there are 366 days. 366 days make 52 weeks and 2 days left over. Two days after Saturday is Monday, so 15th August 2016 was a Monday.

stepByStep.text: From 1st April 2003 to 1st April 2004 is one full year. The year 2004 is a leap year and its 29th of February comes before 1st April, so this stretch has 366 days.
A week has 7 days. 366 days make 52 full weeks with 2 days left over.
Full weeks bring us back to the same day, so only the 2 extra days matter. This is the trap: an ordinary year moves the day forward by 1, but the leap day makes it 2.
Two days after Tuesday is Thursday. So in 2004 it was celebrated on Thursday.

misconceptions.A: Monday is one day before Tuesday. The day moves forward, not back, as the years go by, so count on from Tuesday.
misconceptions.B: A date falls on the same day again only when the days in between make full weeks. Here 366 days leave 2 days over, so count 2 days on from Tuesday.
misconceptions.C: Wednesday is what an ordinary year of 365 days would give, moving the day on by 1. Look for the 29th of February 2004 that falls in between.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The leap day in February 2004 makes 366 days, which is 52 weeks and 2 days, and 2 days after Tuesday is Thursday.

questionText: 9th April 1990 was a Monday. Which days occurred five times in that month?

hints: This is a calendar problem. Every month has four full weeks plus a few extra days, and only the days of the week that land on those extra days come five times.

Here is a similar problem. Suppose 12th July is a Friday. Seven days earlier, the 5th is also a Friday, so the 4th is Thursday, the 3rd is Wednesday, the 2nd is Tuesday and the 1st is Monday. stepByStep.text: Counting back 7 days from Monday the 9th gives Monday the 2nd. The day before that, the 1st of April, was a Sunday.
April has 30 days. That is 4 full weeks and 2 days more.
In 4 full weeks every day of the week comes 4 times. The 2 extra days are the 29th and 30th, which fall on the same days as the 1st and 2nd.

misconceptions.B: Yes! 09:45 plus 4 hours is 13:45, and 35 more minutes makes 14:20, which is 2:20 PM.

questionText: How many days are there from 15th August to 2nd October (not counting 15th August)?

questionText: How many seconds are there in 2 hours?

questionText: In the year 2000, Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October) fell on Monday. In which year was it first celebrated on Sunday after 2000?
hints: This is a calendar problem. The same date moves forward one day of the week after an ordinary year, and two days when a 29th of February falls in between. Follow the date year by year.

Start from Monday in 2000 and find the day for 2nd October 2001. The leap day of 2000 came in February, before October, so check whether any 29th of February lies between October 2000 and October 2001.

Here is a similar problem. 5th July 2010 was a Monday, and we want the first later year when 5th July fell on a Friday. In 2011 it was Tuesday. In 2012 it was Thursday, because 29th February 2012 falls in between and moves it 2 days. In 2013 it was Friday. So the year is 2013.

The leap day of 2000 was in February, before October, so it does not count here. In 2001 the day was Tuesday, in 2002 Wednesday and in 2003 Thursday.
Between October 2003 and October 2004 comes 29th February 2004. That stretch has 366 days, so the day jumps 2 days, from Thursday to Saturday. This is the trap: Friday is skipped.
One more ordinary year moves Saturday on to Sunday. So it was first celebrated on Sunday in 2005.

misconceptions.A: In 2004 the day jumped from Thursday to Saturday because of the leap day, so 2nd October 2004 was a Saturday. Go one more year.
misconceptions.B: By 2003 the day had moved on only 3 days from Monday, to Thursday. Keep counting year by year.
misconceptions.C: Excellent thinking! The leap day of 2004 made the day jump to Saturday, and one more year brought it to Sunday in 2005.
misconceptions.D: 2006 comes from moving one day every year for six years. The leap day of February 2004 makes one step a jump of 2 days, so Sunday arrives a year earlier.
